description:
FILED s507b (Opus, 2026-10-04) from member 1's (#2680) breaking-case probes; PRE-EXISTING on main 08de9e4f.

REPRODUCER:
  sub bb { {; } }  my @bb = (bb(), 1);  print scalar(@bb), "\n";
  perl: 1   (perlfunc map / perlref: a `{` followed by `;` is always a BLOCK)
  PCL : 2   (emission `(p-args-body (block nil (make-p-box (p-hash))))` -- a hash ref)
`sub nest { { } }` IS an anon hash in perl too (2 elements, matched by PCL); `sub b0 { { (); } }` is a block (1 element,
matched since s507b).  The `{;` spelling is the documented way to force a block (`map {; "$_" => 1 } @l` is the
canonical case) -- probe that one too: it is far more common than this reproducer.
CHEAP MEASUREMENT (not taken): `./pl2cl` on `my @l = map {; "$_" => 1 } 1, 2; print scalar(@l)` -- if it emits a
hash constructor, the brace classifier (Pl::PExpr::_block_is_hash_constructor / _block_is_empty, or PPI's own
Structure::Constructor vs Block choice) ignores a leading `;`.  If PPI hands back a Constructor, it is a PPI bug for
docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md (rule 13).


=== DONE (s507c, built s508, shipped s509) ===
Not a PPI bug: PPI gives a Structure::Block; PCL's _normalize_null_statements DELETED the sole Null, leaving `{}`, which every term classifier reads as an anon hash.  A SOLE Null in a block now becomes `();` (reparse) -- a block by the same classifiers.  `{; ;}`, `{;}` after statements, `sub f {;}`, `if (1) {;}`, `while (...) {;}`, `map {;} LIST` and `map {; "$_" => 1 }` all = perl; `{ }` stays an anon hash.  Guard: transpile-test-10.t last row.
Review F2 (Fable s509): `{; a => 1 }` STARTING a statement also lost its `;` and read as an anon hash; the leading `;` now becomes `();` there (deref blocks and blocks after map/do keep the deletion).  Probed = perl: b3/b4/b5/b6/b7, `{ a => 1 }` and `+{ a => 1 }` stay HASH refs, `{;}` empty list, map {;...}, ${; "z"}, a bare `{; print }`.  Guard transpile-test-10.t F2 row.  Fable lv.pl: 65 of 66 = perl (d2, a slice in scalar context, is not this task).
subject: SILENT WRONG (PRE-EXISTING): `{;` -- perl's explicit BLOCK disambiguator -- is read as an anonymous HASH: `sub f { {; } }` returns a hash ref where perl returns the empty list
